claims.text: Verbatim, sec. 9010(a) of Division G of S. 2226 as engrossed in the Senate: 'Exercise of Eminent Domain.--The Federal Government shall exercise eminent domain over any and all recovered technologies of unknown origin and biological evidence of non-human intelligence that may be controlled by private persons or entities in the interests of the public good.'

The full section is titled 'DISCLOSURE OF RECOVERED TECHNOLOGIES OF UNKNOWN ORIGIN AND BIOLOGICAL EVIDENCE OF NON-HUMAN INTELLIGENCE' and has five subsections: (a) exercise of eminent domain; (b) availability to Review Board; (c) actions of Review Board; (d) Review Board access to testimony and witnesses; (e) solicitation of additional witnesses.

Sec. 9010(b) conditions the taking on location: material 'shall be made available to the Review Board for personal examination and subsequent disclosure determination at a location suitable to the controlling authority of said material' - the bill contemplates a private or non-governmental 'controlling authority' holding the material.
Sec. 9010 was not enacted. It appears in the Senate-engrossed text of S. 2226 and in the Congressional Record text of S.Amdt. 797 (13 July 2023); it has no counterpart in Public Law 118-31.

claims.text: An eminent domain power drafted to run only against 'private persons or entities' is a statement about where the drafters believed the material was, not merely a precaution; the Government has no need to condemn property it already owns.

desc: The single most important sentence in the modern disclosure record, and a Tier 1 documented fact whose existence does not depend on believing any witness. Section 9010 of Division G of S. 2226, headed 'Disclosure of Recovered Technologies of Unknown Origin and Biological Evidence of Non-Human Intelligence,' opens: 'The Federal Government shall exercise eminent domain over any and all recovered technologies of unknown origin and biological evidence of non-human intelligence that may be controlled by private persons or entities in the interests of the public good.' Subsection (b) requires that 'any and all such material, should it exist, shall be made available to the Review Board for personal examination and subsequent disclosure determination at a location suitable to the controlling authority of said material.' Subsection (c) directs the Board to decide 'whether the material examined constitutes technologies of unknown origin or biological evidence of non-human intelligence beyond a reasonable doubt.' The drafting is careful and revealing in both directions: the hedge 'should it exist' preserves deniability, while 'shall exercise' is mandatory and the taking is aimed exclusively at private holders, not at Government agencies — the Government does not need eminent domain against itself. A chamber of Congress passed this. It was then deleted, and the deletion is the fact that organises this entire domain.

entityInfo.desc:
Full text as passed by the Senate, 27 July 2023, S. 2226 Division G:

SEC. 9010. DISCLOSURE OF RECOVERED TECHNOLOGIES OF UNKNOWN ORIGIN AND BIOLOGICAL EVIDENCE OF NON-HUMAN INTELLIGENCE.
(a) Exercise of Eminent Domain.--The Federal Government shall exercise eminent domain over any and all recovered technologies of unknown origin and biological evidence of non-human intelligence that may be controlled by private persons or entities in the interests of the public good.
(b) Availability to Review Board.--Any and all such material, should it exist, shall be made available to the Review Board for personal examination and subsequent disclosure determination at a location suitable to the controlling authority of said material and in a timely manner conducive to the objectives of the Review Board in accordance with the requirements of this division.
(c) Actions of Review Board.--In carrying out subsection (b), the Review Board shall consider and render decisions-- (1) whether the material examined constitutes technologies of unknown origin or biological evidence of non-human intelligence beyond a reasonable doubt; (2) whether recovered technologies of unknown origin, biological evidence of non-human intelligence, or a particular subset of material qualifies for postponement of disclosure under this division...

label: Section 9010(a) — Exercise of Eminent Domain
